title: Telling the supplier, and marking it confirmed

Reply.dc.html.title: Asked — and the reply is the act

NowDialog.dc.html.title: Now · the button that does nothing

NowModal.dc.html.title: Now · the panel nobody can reach

nA.text:
TAKEN IS THE STAGE WHERE AN ORDER WAITS ON PEOPLE.

So at Taken the right-hand pane stops being a list of lines and becomes a set of SUPPLIERS — because the question the screen is being asked has changed. “What is on it” is the Buying question. “Who has it, and have they said yes” is this one.

Each supplier is the same card the buying round already uses: a place, what it is worth, what is on it, its state, and one act. Three screens, one card.

nB.text:
THE ACCENT SITS ON WHOSEVER TURN IT IS.

Before anybody has been asked, the only meaningful act is “Ask them”. Once they have been asked, the next thing anybody does is record what they said — so the accent moves to “They confirmed”, on the one card that is next. Every other card’s acts are ghosts.

That is how the screen keeps one oxide while still making the thing the user asked for — marking it confirmed after telling them — the most prominent act on it.

nC.text:
WHAT THEY SAID, TYPED IN WHEN THEY SAID IT.

“No stock till Friday” and “the price is 12,000 now” lead to completely different fixes, and by the time anybody reads the card the call is forgotten. The reason is on the card, in the supplier’s own words.

The mark never carries state by colour alone: a NUMBER while we are still asking, a TICK once they have said yes, a BANG when they have said no.

nD.text:
THE BUG.

The red button says “Suppliers”. Pressing it calls otOpenRow, which expands that order’s row on the board — behind the dialog’s own full-screen scrim, in a table far below the lanes. The dialog stays open, its body is byte-identical, and nothing appears to happen.

It is not that nothing runs. It is that what runs is invisible.

nE.text:
AND THE PANEL ALREADY EXISTS.

This is what the button was promising: ask on WhatsApp, they confirmed, report a problem — per supplier, with the lines written out word for word as the message will say them.

It works. Its only door is a button inside that invisible row. And because a modal sat at z-index 100 under the dialog’s 120, opening it from the dialog would have drawn it UNDERNEATH anyway.

So the design does not replace it. It moves it to the stage it is about, and keeps every act it already had.
